> **MUST** `ship-safely`: Never push to the main branch. Every change goes through a review.

> **MUST NOT** `no-false-claims`: Say something works unless you ran it and saw it work.

> **Note:** This skill is a demo of the template features, built around a realistic workflow.

House style for the checkout service: small commits, plain language, and a test for every fix.

> **CUSTOM COMPONENT:** This one comes from `components/DemoBadge.md`, next to this template.

## Track the work
<!-- anchor: track-work -->

Keep a visible task list for this work, so that the user can see where things stand without asking.

Use `TaskCreate` to add each step and `TaskUpdate` to change its status. Claude Code shows the list live. On some models these tools must be switched on, so if you do not have them, use the fallback below.

- Create the list before you start, with one item per step the user would recognize.
- Mark an item in progress when you begin it, and done as soon as it is finished, never in batches at the end.
- Keep exactly one item in progress at a time.
- If the plan changes, change the list in the same step.

Start with these items:

- Settle the details with the user
- Get the plan approved
- Build and review it
- Open the pull request

Two exceptions:

- **If you have no task list tool:** keep a Markdown checklist (`- [ ]` and `- [x]`) and repeat it whenever it changes.
- **If you are a subagent:** keep your list short, and include its final state in your report.

## Step A: name the feature
<!-- anchor: name-feature -->

**Ask the user:** What should this feature's flag and branch be called?

This needs the user's own words, such as a name, a path or a description, which a list of options cannot offer.

Ask in your reply, as one clear question, and end your turn. `AskUserQuestion` is built for choices, so use it only if a few likely answers are worth offering, since it always lets the user type their own.
Give an example of the form you want: faster-checkout

- Ask for one thing at a time, and say what you will do with the answer.
- If you can find the answer yourself, do that instead of asking.
- **If you are a subagent:** you cannot reach the user. Report what you need, and why.

## Step B: choose an approach
<!-- anchor: choose-approach -->

**Ask the user:** How should I build this feature?

Show this as a single-choice list that the user selects from, not as a question in your reply.

Use the `AskUserQuestion` tool. It takes 1 to 4 questions, each with a `header` of at most 12 characters and 2 to 4 options. Each option has a `label` of 1 to 5 words and a `description`. It adds an "Other" choice by itself, so do not add one.
Set `multiSelect: false`, so that exactly one option can be chosen.

Offer these options:

- Smallest change (Recommended): touch as little as possible
- Refactor first: clean the area up, then add the feature
- Feature flag: ship it switched off

- Put the option you recommend first, and add "(Recommended)" to its label.
- Options must exclude each other. If several could be true together, this is the wrong question type.
- After asking, stop and wait. Do not assume an answer or carry on without one.
- **If you have no question tool:** write a numbered list, ask for one number, and end your turn.
- **If you are a subagent:** you cannot reach the user. Use the smallest change that works, and say so in your report.

## Step C: choose the API style
<!-- anchor: choose-api -->

**Ask the user:** Which API style reads best here?

The options look different and the user has to see them to choose, such as layouts, code styles or output formats. Show each one.

Use the `AskUserQuestion` tool. It takes 1 to 4 questions, each with a `header` of at most 12 characters and 2 to 4 options. Each option has a `label` of 1 to 5 words and a `description`. It adds an "Other" choice by itself, so do not add one.
If the tool offers a `preview` field on its options, put each option's example there. Previews need a single-choice question. Whether this field is offered depends on the session's settings.

Offer these options:

- Options object: `pay({ amount, currency })`
- Plain arguments: `pay(amount, currency)`

- Make each preview real: a code snippet, a small ASCII mockup or a sample of the output.
- Keep previews about the same length, so that they compare fairly.
- **If the tool has no previews:** put each option in your reply, under its own label with its example in a code block, and then ask which one the user wants.
- After asking, stop and wait.
- **If you are a subagent:** choose the option that best fits the task, and report your choice with its example.

## Step D: choose the checks
<!-- anchor: choose-checks -->

**Ask the user:** Which checks should I run before review?

Show this as a checkbox list, where the user can tick any number of options, not as a question in your reply.

Use the `AskUserQuestion` tool. It takes 1 to 4 questions, each with a `header` of at most 12 characters and 2 to 4 options. Each option has a `label` of 1 to 5 words and a `description`. It adds an "Other" choice by itself, so do not add one.
Set `multiSelect: true`, so that several options can be chosen.

Offer these options:

- Unit tests
- Lint
- Security scan

- Phrase the question so that choosing several makes sense, such as "Which of these should I include?"
- At least 1 must be chosen. If fewer are, ask again.
- Options must be independent, so that any combination is valid. If some exclude each other, ask them separately.
- After asking, stop and wait. Do not assume an answer or carry on without one.
- **If you have no question tool, or it has no multi-select:** write a numbered list, ask for all the numbers that apply, separated by commas, and end your turn.
- **If you are a subagent:** you cannot reach the user. Choose only what the task clearly requires, and report those choices to the agent that started you.

## Step E: settle the details
<!-- anchor: choose-settings -->

Ask related questions together in a **single call**, so that they appear as tabs the user can move between before submitting. Do not ask them one at a time, and do not ask them in your reply.

Use the `AskUserQuestion` tool. It takes 1 to 4 questions, each with a `header` of at most 12 characters and 2 to 4 options. Each option has a `label` of 1 to 5 words and a `description`. It adds an "Other" choice by itself, so do not add one.
Put every question in the `questions` array of one call, each with its own short `header`, which is the tab's label. Set `multiSelect` for each question on its own.

Ask these:

- **Rollout**: How should it roll out? *(one can be chosen)*
  All at once (Recommended), or gradually

- **Docs**: Which docs need updating? *(several can be chosen)*
  README, or the changelog, or the API reference

- Ask at most 4 together. For more, group the related ones and make a second call only after the first is answered.
- Each question must stand on its own, because the user may answer them in any order.
- After asking, stop and wait for all the answers. Do not assume any of them.
- **If you have no question tool:** write the questions as numbered sections with lettered options, ask for answers in the form `1: a, 2: b c`, and end your turn.
- **If you are a subagent:** you cannot reach the user. Answer each one with the recommended option, and report your choices to the agent that started you.

## Step F: get the plan approved
<!-- anchor: approve-plan -->

Do not change anything until the user has approved a plan.

Call `EnterPlanMode` before you start. Investigate without changing files, then present your plan with `ExitPlanMode`, which asks the user to approve it.

The plan must cover:

- The answers from steps A to E
- The checks you will run, and in what order

- Say which files will change, how you will verify the result, and what could go wrong.
- If the user asks for changes, revise the plan and ask again. Do not start on a partial approval.
- **If you have no plan mode:** write the plan as a numbered list, ask for approval, and end your turn.
- **If you are a subagent:** you cannot get approval, so report your plan and change nothing, unless your task says to make the changes.

## Subagents
<!-- anchor: subagents -->

Decide per piece of work, using these rules. If neither rule applies, do the work yourself.

- **Use a subagent when:** the work splits into independent parts, or needs broad searching
- **Do not use a subagent when:** the steps depend on each other
- **Run at most 3 at once.** Wait for one to finish before starting another.

If your harness has no way to run subagents, do the work in order yourself and say so once.

## Step G: build it: research, build, review
<!-- anchor: build-flow -->

You are the orchestrator. Run the stages below in order, and delegate each one to a subagent. Keep your own work to coordinating and checking results, so that your context stays clear.

- **Give each subagent everything it needs.** It starts with none of this conversation, so its prompt must state the goal, the inputs, the exact output you want, and when to stop.
- **Do not guess a subagent's result.** Wait for it, read it, and check it against the stage's "Done when" before moving on.
- **Run a stage in parallel only if it says so.** Parallel subagents must not change the same files.
- **Subagents cannot reach the user.** Questions that need the user are for you to ask between stages. A subagent makes a reasonable choice, and reports it.
- **If a stage fails,** retry it once with what you learned added to the prompt. If it fails again, stop and report what happened, rather than continuing on a bad result.
- **If your harness cannot run subagents,** do each stage yourself, in order, and say so once.

### Stage 1: Research
<!-- anchor: research -->

**Run up to 3 subagents at once.**

Find the code this feature touches.

**Output:** Short findings with file paths, and no changes to any file

**Done when:** you could explain the change, with evidence for each claim

### Stage 2: Build
<!-- anchor: build -->

Make the change the user chose in step B.

**Output:** The changes made, and how they were checked

**Done when:** the code is changed and the tests pass

### Stage 3: Review
<!-- anchor: review -->

**Subagent:** a fresh subagent that did not write the code
Look for bugs in the changes.

**Output:** Real problems, each with a file, a line and why it matters

**Done when:** each problem is fixed, or you have explained why it stays

When every stage is done, combine the results and report them yourself. Never pass a subagent's text on unchecked.

## Step G2: split the build, if it allows
<!-- anchor: split-work -->

Use this to split one piece of work among subagents **in this working tree**. They share files, and there is no merge step to catch a collision, so the plan decides what may run together, not your judgment.

1. **List the jobs.** Write each one down with every file it will change, as a file or a directory ending in `/`. Add `reads` for files it relies on staying the same. Be honest and include what is easy to forget: tests, and shared files such as lockfiles, generated code and indexes. A job that changes files you cannot predict gets `exclusive: true`, and `deps` say what must finish first.

   ```yaml
   jobs:
     - id: api
       touches: [internal/api/users.go]
     - id: docs
       touches: [docs/users.md]
       reads: [internal/api/users.go]
     - id: format
       exclusive: true
       deps: [api, docs]
   ```

2. **Get the plan.**

   ```sh
   aiculator parallel plan --file jobs.yaml --max 3 --granularity auto -o plan.json
   ```

   If it says `Sequential`, do the jobs yourself, one at a time. Do not run them together anyway. Do not reword the jobs to get a different answer. Two jobs in one file conflict, because two subagents editing one file can overwrite each other, and naming parts of the file does not change that.

3. **For each wave, in order:**
   1. Record the state: `aiculator parallel snapshot`, and keep what it prints.
   2. Start one subagent per job in that wave, all in the same turn.
   3. Wait for every one of them.
   4. Check them: `aiculator parallel verify --plan plan.json --wave N --since SNAPSHOT`.
   5. If it reports files no job claimed, stop. Look at what changed, fix it yourself, and do not start the next wave until the tree is right.
   6. If it lists a job that changed nothing, check whether that subagent really did its work.
   7. Run the tests before the next wave.

**Tell every subagent, in its prompt:**

- Exactly which files it may change, and that it must change nothing else, even to fix something it notices. It reports that to you instead.
- To read a file again just before changing it, and to make small, targeted edits rather than rewriting the file.
- Not to run `git add`, `git commit`, `git stash`, `git checkout` or `git reset`, formatters over the whole project, or anything that installs dependencies. Others are working in the same tree.
- Not to call any swarm tools. A lease belongs to you, and only you report progress or submit.

- **If your harness cannot run subagents,** do the jobs yourself, in the planned order.
- **If you are a subagent yourself,** do not start more. Do your own part, and report back.
- **For separate tasks that take a long time,** use the swarm's own worktrees instead, because those can also be reviewed and merged one by one.

## Commands: timeouts and retries
<!-- anchor: backoff -->

Give every command a time limit of **120s**. A command that hits the limit has failed; do not wait longer.

Retry only for: timeouts, network errors and rate limits.
Do not retry a failure that will repeat, such as a failing test, a syntax error or a denied permission. Read the error and change something first.

| Attempt | Wait before it |
|---|---|
| 1 | None |
| 2 | 2s |
| 3 | 4s |
| 4 | 8s |

After the last attempt, stop retrying. Report the command, the final error and what you tried.

## Checks to run
<!-- anchor: checks -->

1. Run unit tests, and stop if it fails.
2. Run lint, and stop if it fails.
3. Run security scan, and stop if it fails.

## Flow: ship it
<!-- anchor: ship-flow -->

Do these steps in order, one at a time. Do not skip a step or merge steps, except as stated here. After each step, say which step you finished and which comes next.

- **Steps marked "Ask the user":** ask, then stop and wait for the answer. Use your harness's question tool if it has one, and otherwise end your turn with the question. Do not guess the answer or continue without it.
- **If you are a subagent:** you were started by another agent and cannot reach the user. Follow the "As a subagent" line in each step instead of asking. Report every default you chose to the agent that started you.

### Step 1: Confirm
<!-- anchor: confirm -->

Summarize what changed and what you checked.

**Ask the user:** Is this ready to ship?

**As a subagent:** Do not ask. Report that it is ready, with your evidence.

### Step 2: Ship
<!-- anchor: ship -->

Open the pull request.

**As a subagent:** Do not ship. Only the agent that started you does that.

## Step H: clean up
<!-- anchor: delete-branch -->

**Ask the user:** Delete the merged feature branch?

Ask this as a yes or no choice, and do not continue until you have the answer.

Use the `AskUserQuestion` tool, with `multiSelect: false` and two options: the action, named specifically, and a way to decline.

- Name what will happen in the option itself, such as "Delete 3 branches", not just "Yes".
- Say what cannot be undone.
- Silence is not a yes. If the answer is unclear, ask again.
- **If you have no question tool:** ask for a clear yes or no, and end your turn.
- **If you are a subagent:** do not take the action. Report that it needs confirmation.

## Output format
<!-- anchor: output-format -->

Every reply must use exactly this format, including short ones and replies late in a long session. Before you send a reply, compare it with this format and fix any difference.

```text
Done: what changed
Checked: what you ran and the result
Next: what remains, or "nothing"
```

## Progress
<!-- anchor: progress -->

**This section is alive: keep it true.** Update it after each step above. Treat a stale section as a bug.

- Change only what lies between the markers, and leave the markers themselves in place.
- Replace what is out of date instead of adding to it, so that this always reads as the present state and never as a history.
- It must always cover: the current step, and anything blocking it.
- If you are a subagent, report what should change to the agent that started you, unless you were told to edit it.

<!-- dynamic:progress:start -->
Not started.
<!-- dynamic:progress:end -->

## Release notes
<!-- anchor: changelog -->

**This section is alive: keep it true.** Update it whenever the plan changes. Treat a stale section as a bug.

It lives in `RELEASE_NOTES.md`, between the marker comments `<!-- dynamic:changelog:start -->` and `<!-- dynamic:changelog:end -->`. Create the file and markers if they do not exist yet.

- Change only what lies between the markers, and leave the markers themselves in place.
- Replace what is out of date instead of adding to it, so that this always reads as the present state and never as a history.
- If you are a subagent, report what should change to the agent that started you, unless you were told to edit it.

## How to format your replies
<!-- anchor: formatting -->

Choose the form that makes each thing easiest to read, using the rules below. Do not decorate: a short answer in a plain sentence is often best, and formatting should never replace a clear explanation.

This output goes to a terminal. Assume code blocks and tables work, and that diagrams, images, collapsible sections and LaTeX may not.

### Code
<!-- anchor: render-code -->

Put all code in a fenced block with a language, so that it is highlighted and easy to copy. Never indent it instead. Say which file it belongs to on the line above.

````markdown
In `internal/calc.go`:

```go
func add(a, b int) int { return a + b }
```
````

### Commands
<!-- anchor: render-shell -->

Give commands in a `sh` block that can be pasted as it is: no `$` prompt, and one step per line. Show their output in a separate `text` block. Say beforehand if a command changes anything.

```sh
go test ./...
```

### Changes
<!-- anchor: render-diff -->

To show a change to code, use a `diff` block with just enough context to place it.

```diff
-func add(a, b int) int { return a - b }
+func add(a, b int) int { return a + b }
```

### Tables
<!-- anchor: render-table -->

Use a table to compare items across two or more attributes. Keep cells to a few words, put explanations in the text around it, and right-align numbers. Do not use a table for a plain list, or for one row.

```markdown
| Option | Speed | Cost |
|---|--:|--:|
| A | 12 ms | $3 |
| B | 40 ms | $1 |
```

### Checklists
<!-- anchor: render-checklist -->

Show progress or remaining steps as a checklist.

```markdown
- [x] Add the endpoint
- [ ] Write the tests
```

### Callouts
<!-- anchor: render-callout -->

Set off a warning or key note as a quote, starting with a bold label. Use this only for what the reader must not miss, and rarely.

```markdown
> **Warning:** This deletes the production table.
```

### File trees
<!-- anchor: render-tree -->

Show a directory layout in a `text` block, using box-drawing characters.

```text
cmd/
├── main.go
└── serve.go
```

### Diagrams
<!-- anchor: render-diagram -->

A terminal may show Mermaid as plain source, so draw flows as ASCII in a `text` block. Use a Mermaid block only when the user asks, or when the answer is going into a document that renders it.

```text
Request --> Valid? --yes--> Save
              |
              no--> Reject
```

### Images
<!-- anchor: render-image -->

A terminal may not show images, so give the file's path and say what it shows. Do not rely on an image to carry the point.

### Collapsible sections
<!-- anchor: render-details -->

A terminal may show `<details>` tags as plain text, so do not use them. Leave optional material out and offer it, or put it at the end under its own heading.

### File references
<!-- anchor: render-fileref -->

Refer to code as `path/to/file.go:42`, with the line number, because many harnesses make this clickable. Use the path from the project root, and do not wrap it in a link.

In this demo, cite the checkout code this way in every review finding.

<!-- anchor: render-details -->

A terminal may show `<details>` tags as plain text, so do not use them. Leave optional material out and offer it, or put it at the end under its own heading.

### File references
<!-- anchor: render-fileref -->

Refer to code as `path/to/file.go:42`, with the line number, because many harnesses make this clickable. Use the path from the project root, and do not wrap it in a link.

In this demo, cite the checkout code this way in every review finding.

docs.title: Every feature, and what it does
docs.text:
• Jinja2

    Variables, conditions, loops, macros, filters, comments and includes. A typo in a variable name is an error.

  • Question types

    A list, checkboxes, tabs, yes or no, free text or previews, using the harness's real tool.

  • Subagent flows

    Stages with inputs, outputs and a check before moving on.

  • Retries

    A timeout and a retry table the swarm computes for the model.

  • Flows

    Ordered steps, with questions and exceptions for subagents.

  • Live sections

    Text a model keeps true. A re-render keeps what it wrote.

  • Task lists and plans

    A live task list, and a plan the user approves first.

  • Rich Markdown

    Rules for 19 Markdown forms, adjusted for terminals.

Jinja2QuestionsWorkflowRich MarkdownNavigation and rules Feature Where in the demo Effect template: vars: Frontmatter Defaults that --set overrides, removed from the output {{ project }} The title A variable {# ... #} Throughout A comment that never reaches the skill {% macro %} check_row A reusable piece, called from a loop {% if %} The first line Differs per harness {% for %} "Step D" and "Checks to run" Repeats for each item {% include %} House style Shared text from another file capitalize "Step D" A filter, written after a pipe inside {{ }} Component Where The model is told to <AskText> Step A Ask for the user's own words <AskOne> Step B Ask for exactly one choice <AskPreview> Step C Show an example of each option <AskMany> Step D Offer checkboxes, with min for at least one <AskTabs> and <Tab> Step E Ask everything in one call <AskConfirm> Step H Get a yes or no before a risky action

Each also says what to do with no question tool, and what a subagent should do instead of asking. Set that with subagent="...".

Component Where The model is told to <TodoList> "Track the work" Keep a live task list <PlanMode> Step F Get a plan approved before changing anything <Subagents> Before step G Use subagents only in these cases <SubagentFlow> and <Stage> Step G Orchestrate stages, checking each result <ParallelWork> Step G2 Plan subagents in one worktree, and verify each wave <Backoff> After step G Limit commands, and retry on this schedule <Flow> and <Step> "Ship it" Follow steps in order, one at a time <OutputFormat> Near the end Use this format in every reply Component Where The model is told to <RichMarkdown> "How to format your replies" Follow the rules for each form, with only choosing which ones <Render> "File references" Follow one rule, with your own advice added as the tag's content

Set surface to terminal or rich. Try --set surface=rich to see diagrams and collapsible sections change. See Forcing rich Markdown for all 19 kinds.

Component Where Effect <Toc depth="2" /> Top Contents with exact line numbers and anchors, for ## sections only <Anchor> "Checks to run" A searchable marker <Directive> Top A rule the model can cite by name <Note> Top A callout <DynamicSection> The last two Text the model keeps current, in the skill or in another file <DemoBadge> Top Your own component

docs.title: Anatomy of a component
docs.text:
<AskOne id="choose-approach" question="How should I build this feature?" subagent="Use the smallest change.">
- Smallest change (Recommended): touch as little as possible
- Refactor first: clean the area up
</AskOne>
Part What it does id Becomes the anchor in the contents list, so a model can jump straight here question Props become variables inside the component, and can use values from Jinja2, which runs first subagent Says what a subagent should do instead, since it cannot reach the user The tag's content Becomes children. Put your recommendation first Why two passes, Jinja2 and then components?

Jinja2 runs first, so <Backoff retries="{{ retries }}" /> receives a real number. Components then expand, innermost first, so a <Tab> is ready by the time <AskTabs> uses it. The contents list comes last, because only then are the line numbers known.

What happens to tags in code examples?

They are left alone. The <Flow> in a code fence or in inline code stays exactly as written, so a skill can show examples of them.

Do these force a model to behave?

No. They are instructions, and a model can still ignore text. On a real model the question types, task lists, plans, formatting rules, the subagent flow and live sections all worked as intended, which you can check with scripts/gate_ui_templates.sh. Anything that must hold needs a real check, such as a task's --check command.

docs.title: Make your own
docs.text:
• Copy .agent/template/demo.mdx to a new name, and change name: to match
  • Keep the components you need, and delete the rest
  • Preview with aiculator template --render NAME
  • Install with aiculator template --install NAME
  • Add aiculator template --check to CI, so that a changed template cannot go stale unnoticed

Or start smaller with aiculator template --new my-rules. See Templates for the full reference.

docs.title: Templates
docs.text:
Templates let you write instructions once and reuse them. Use them for the rules you keep repeating: when to use subagents, how to retry, what format to reply in, and which steps to follow.

Instructions, not enforcement

A template produces text for a model, and a model can still ignore text. Clear, specific rules are followed far more often, but anything that must hold needs a real check, such as a task's --check command.

See every feature working together

The template demo walks through one template that uses all of this.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
aiculator template --list
aiculator template --render agent-discipline --set retries=5   # Preview; writes nothing
aiculator template --install agent-discipline                  # Render and install

--install takes the same options as skill --install: patterns, --harness, --global, --path and --copy.

docs.title: Where templates live
docs.text:
Templates go in .agents/templates/. .agent/templates/ and .agent/template/ also work.

.agents/templates/
├── my-rules.md.j2            # A single-file template
├── release-flow/             # A template with extra files
│   ├── SKILL.md.j2
│   └── references/guide.md   # Copied into the skill
├── partials/                 # For {% include %}
└── components/               # Your own <Components>

Single files can end in .md.j2, .j2, .jinja or .mdx.

docs.title: Anatomy of a template
docs.text:
---
template:                 # Removed from the output
  vars:
    retries: 3
name: my-rules
description: Working rules for this project. Use when the user asks to apply them.
metadata:
  version: "1.0.0"
---

# My rules

<Toc />

<Directive id="main-rule">Never push to main.</Directive>

{% if harness.id == "claude" %}
This line appears only in the Claude Code copy.
{% endif %}

{% include "partials/house-style.md" %}

<Backoff timeout="120s" retries="{{ retries }}" />

Rendering runs in two passes: Jinja2 first, then components. So {{ retries }} can feed a component's props.

docs.title: Subagents
docs.text:
Says when to use subagents.

<Subagents use="when" max="4"
  when="the work splits into independent parts"
  not_when="the steps depend on each other" />

use is always, when or never.

docs.title: Backoff
docs.text:
Sets a command timeout and a retry policy. The swarm computes the table of waits, because a model told to "double it each time" tends to get the numbers wrong.

<Backoff timeout="120s" retries="3" base="2s" factor="2" limit="60s" />

Add on="..." to say which failures to retry.

docs.title: OutputFormat
docs.text:
Makes the model repeat a format in every reply.

<OutputFormat>
Done: what changed
Checked: what you ran and the result
</OutputFormat>

Use repeat="Final answers" to apply it to only some replies.

docs.title: Flow and Step
docs.text:
Forces an order of steps, with interactive questions and exceptions for subagents, which cannot reach the user.

<Flow name="confirm before acting" id="confirm-flow">
<Step n="1" title="Plan" id="plan"
  ask="Does this plan look right?"
  subagent="Do not ask. Continue, and report your plan with the result.">
List the changes you intend to make.
</Step>
</Flow>

docs.title: Directive
docs.text:
Marks a rule the model can cite by name. level is any word, and defaults to must.

<Directive level="must not" id="no-false-claims">Say something works unless you ran it.</Directive>

docs.title: Toc and Anchor
docs.text:
<Toc /> writes a table of contents with exact line numbers and anchors, so a model can jump to a section without reading the whole file:

## Contents

- Subagents: line 28, anchor `subagents`
- Commands: timeouts and retries: line 39, anchor `backoff`

<Anchor id="name" /> adds a searchable marker anywhere. Most components add their own.

docs.title: Note
docs.text: <Note>Something worth pointing out.</Note>

docs.title: Forcing a kind of question
docs.text:
Bundled templates tell a model which interface to use, so you get a list to select from, and not a paragraph to answer.

Template Component What the user sees ui-select <AskOne> One choice from a list ui-checkbox <AskMany> Any number of choices, as checkboxes ui-tabs <AskTabs> and <Tab> Several questions in one form, with tabs ui-confirm <AskConfirm> A yes or no choice before a risky action ui-text <AskText> A place to type, when options cannot cover the answer ui-preview <AskPreview> Choices with a visible example of each ui-todos <TodoList> A live task list ui-plan <PlanMode> A plan to approve before anything changes 
aiculator template --install 'ui-*'
aiculator template --install 'ui-*' --per-harness --harness claude,opencode   # Names the exact tool

They name the harness's real tool and settings when it has one, and that comes from each harness's docs:

Harness Questions Task list Plan mode Claude Code AskUserQuestion, with multiSelect TaskCreate, TaskUpdate EnterPlanMode, ExitPlanMode Gemini CLI ask_user, with type choice, text or yesno write_todos enter_plan_mode, exit_plan_mode OpenCode question; its docs do not state multi-select todowrite None in its tool docs Others None named: a numbered list, then stop and wait A Markdown checklist A numbered plan, then stop and wait

On some Claude Code models the task tools must be switched on, so ui-todos also tells the model what to do without them. Whether AskUserQuestion offers preview depends on the session, so <AskPreview> falls back to labeled code blocks.

ui-plan deliberately has no allowed-tools. In Claude Code that field skips the permission prompt, and the prompt on ExitPlanMode is your approval of the plan.

Without --per-harness, one shared skill names all three tools, because it cannot know which harness reads it.

To ask a specific question, use the components in your own template:

<AskOne question="Which database?" subagent="Use SQLite, and say so in your report.">
- PostgreSQL (Recommended): best for most apps
- SQLite: no server to run
</AskOne>

<AskMany question="Which checks should I run?" min="1">
- Unit tests
- Security scan
</AskMany>

<AskTabs>
<Tab header="Language" question="Which language?">Go, or Python</Tab>
<Tab header="Extras" question="Which extras?" multi="true">Docker, or CI</Tab>
</AskTabs>

<AskConfirm question="Delete 3 merged branches?" />

<AskText question="What should the service be called?" placeholder="my-service" />

<AskPreview question="Which layout?">
- Compact: `a | b`
- Spacious: `a  |  b`
</AskPreview>

<TodoList>
- Write the tests
- Make them pass
</TodoList>

<PlanMode>
- Which files change
- How you will verify it
</PlanMode>

Every question also covers two cases: a harness with no question tool, and a subagent that cannot reach the user.

docs.title: Forcing rich Markdown
docs.text:
rich-markdown sets how a model formats its replies, using the right form for each thing. <RichMarkdown> includes every rule below, and <Render> adds a single one.

aiculator template --install rich-markdown                    # For a terminal
aiculator template --install rich-markdown --set surface=rich # Where full Markdown renders

<RichMarkdown only="code,diff,table,fileref" surface="terminal" />

<Render kind="callout">Use this for production warnings only.</Render>
kind What the model is told With surface="terminal" (the default) With surface="rich" code Fenced block with a language Same Same inline code, bold and italics, for the right things Same Same shell A sh block to paste, with output apart Same Same diff A diff block Same Same table Comparisons, with short cells Same Same list Numbered when order matters Same Same checklist - [ ] and - [x] Same Same headings ## and ### for longer answers Same Same callout A quote with a bold label Same Also GitHub's > [!WARNING] quote Exact errors, logs and documents Same Same fileref path/to/file.go:42 Same Same tree A directory layout in a text block Same Same link Descriptive text, and only URLs it has seen Same Same diagram Flows and relationships ASCII in a text block A mermaid block image Pictures A path and a description ![alt](path) details Long optional material Left out, or at the end <details> math Formulas Plain text or code $...$ and $$...$$ footnote Asides and sources Short sentences and links [^1] rule Separate parts of a reply Same Same

An unknown kind fails the render, so a typo cannot silently drop a rule.

What this controls, and what it does not

These rules decide what the model writes. How it then looks depends on your harness and where it runs, which most harnesses do not document. Terminal rules are the cautious default for that reason, so check a sample in your own harness before you set surface=rich.

A long skill can keep its contents list short with <Toc depth="2" />, which lists only the ## sections.

docs.title: Subagent flows
docs.text:
subagent-flow makes a model act as an orchestrator: it runs stages in order, delegates each one, and checks each result before moving on.

<SubagentFlow name="research, build, review">
<Stage n="1" title="Research" parallel="3"
  output="Short findings with file paths" done="you could explain the change">
Split the unknowns into separate questions.
</Stage>

<Stage n="2" title="Review" agent="a fresh subagent that did not write the code"
  done="each problem is fixed or explained">
Ask it to look for bugs.
</Stage>
</SubagentFlow>

To split one task among subagents in the same worktree, use the parallel-subagents template or <ParallelWork>. See Parallel subagents.

docs.title: Sections a model keeps current
docs.text:
<DynamicSection> marks text the model must keep true as it works. living-section is a ready-made one, for a progress file.

<DynamicSection id="status" title="Status" file="PROGRESS.md"
  update="after every commit"
  keep="what is done, what is blocked, and the next step" />

With file, the section lives in that project file, which is usually what you want. Without it, the section lives in the skill itself, between markers:

<DynamicSection id="decisions" title="Decisions so far">Nothing yet.</DynamicSection>

Re-rendering keeps what a model wrote there, and --check does not count it as drift. A model's edit can shift the line numbers in a contents list until the next render, though the anchors stay right.

docs.title: How well this works
docs.text:
These are instructions, so a model can still ignore them. scripts/gate_ui_templates.sh tests them on a real Claude Code session, using Haiku, the cheapest model:

Probe Result on the real model ui-select One call with multiSelect: false, recommendation first ui-checkbox One call with multiSelect: true ui-tabs One call holding 3 questions No question tool Looks for the tool, then writes the numbered list As a subagent Does not ask, and reports its choice living-section Writes PROGRESS.md with the markers subagent-flow Three subagents, including a separate reviewer, and the bug fixed ui-confirm One choice, Delete build directory or Keep it, before acting ui-text Asks in its reply, and creates nothing ui-preview Every option carries a preview ui-todos TaskCreate per step, and TaskUpdate as each one starts and ends ui-plan Presents a numbered plan, and changes no file rich-markdown A diff block, a sh block, a table and calc.go:3 in one reply

Print mode has nobody to answer, so Claude Code does not offer AskUserQuestion there. For the mode probes, a small server offers a tool with the same name and schema, and records the arguments. So this proves what the model asks for, but not how the real interactive UI looks. Other harnesses have not been tested this way.

Two more limits follow from this. The ui-plan probe proves the plan comes first and nothing changes, but not the real EnterPlanMode tool, which the model did not call in print mode. The rich-markdown probe checks the text the model wrote, not how a terminal displays it.

docs.title: Your own components
docs.text:
Create components/Name.md in a template directory, using Jinja2. Props become variables, and the tag's content becomes children. A project component with a bundled name replaces the bundled one.

.agents/templates/components/Warn.md
> **Warning{% if topic is defined %} about {{ topic }}{% endif %}:** {{ children | trim }}

<Warn topic="deploys">Check the staging logs first.</Warn>

Tags inside code fences and inline code are left alone, so you can show examples.

docs.title: Per-harness copies
docs.text:
A skill installed the normal way is one file shared through links, so harness.id is generic in it. To vary by harness, render a separate copy into each harness's own directory:

aiculator template --install my-rules --per-harness --harness claude,opencode
aiculator template --render my-rules --for claude     # Preview one
Variable Value harness.id, harness.name Which harness, or generic harness.has_mcp, harness.has_acp What it supports harness.reads_agents Whether it reads .agents/skills harness.question_tool Its question tool, if confirmed; empty otherwise skill.name The template's name aiculator.version The running version

docs.title: Safety
docs.text:
• Rendering cannot run code or read outside the template directories, so rendering a template from an untrusted repository does not endanger your machine. What the skill then tells a model to do still deserves review.
  • A typo in a variable name is an error, and it does not silently render as nothing.
  • A render is linted first. A template with a mistake cannot damage an installed skill.
  • Hand-written skills are never overwritten. Only directories a template generated are replaced.

docs.title: Keep skills current
docs.text:
Rendered skills are ordinary files, so a changed template leaves them stale. This fails if any have drifted, which suits CI:

aiculator template --check

docs.title: Run sandboxed workers
docs.text:
aiculator drive launches a harness for you over the Agent Client Protocol (ACP), one session per task, inside the sandbox.

SWARM_TOKEN=$(aiculator token --agent worker1 --tier 1) \
  aiculator drive --harness claude --agent worker1

docs.title: Why use it
docs.text:
• Idle time costs nothing. No harness runs until there is a task, so waiting uses no model turns.
  • It is sandboxed. The harness can write only to its worktree, a private temp directory and its own state directories. It cannot read the swarm's secrets or credential stores such as ~/.ssh.
  • Permissions follow a policy. Reads, searches and commands are allowed because the sandbox contains them. Edits must stay inside the worktree. Unknown tool kinds are refused.

docs.title: Useful flags
docs.text: Flag Purpose --max-tasks N Stop after N tasks. --manifest file.yaml Use a harness that is not in the registry. --sandbox docker Choose the sandbox. none turns it off, and must be asked for by name. --heartbeat 15s How often to save work and renew the lease. --url The server. By default the project's own, found from .swarm: the driver waits for it if it is not running yet, and finds it again after a restart, a standby taking over, or a move to a new port. --on-limit wait What to do when the harness runs out of usage: wait for the reset it reported, or exit.

docs.title: A custom harness
docs.text:
my-harness.yaml
name: my-harness
command: [my-harness, --acp]
pass_env: [MY_API_KEY]
real_home: true
write_paths: ["~/.my-harness"]
denied_tools: [fetch]

docs.title: When a harness cannot work
docs.text:
A missing login or a failed launch hands the task back with no penalty and stops that driver. It does not use up the task's attempts or move it to a pricier tier.

Running out of plan usage, credit or rate allowance is handled the same way, and the swarm is told. The driver reads it from the harness's errors and stderr: "usage limit reached", "credit balance is too low", insufficient_quota, a 429, and the like. It also reads when the limit resets, if the harness said: a Unix time, an RFC 3339 time, or "try again in 2h 30m". It hands the task back, reports the limit, and by default sleeps until the reset, then carries on. Meanwhile the swarm answers that agent's waits with exit, and aiculator sessions shows it as limited, with when. The agent's own text is held to a stricter test, so that a task about rate limiting or billing doesn't read as the harness running out.

docs.title: Which harnesses have been run
docs.text:
Claude Code and OpenCode have run this way for real. The others are configured from their documentation or the ACP registry and are untested. To test one:

./scripts/gate3_real.sh gemini 3

docs.title: Package managers
docs.text:
Each release runs .github/workflows/packages.yml. Every channel installs the real package first, then publishes it if the release is not a prerelease and the channel's secrets are set. A channel with no secrets is skipped with a notice, and one channel failing does not stop the others.

Current status

Homebrew, Scoop, apt, dnf and apk are live. WinGet is waiting on the review of its first pull request. Chocolatey and the Arch User Repository need the setup below, so their install commands do not work yet.

docs.title: Channels
docs.text:
Channel How it publishes Secrets Needs first Homebrew Commits to your tap PACKAGING_TOKEN Repository homebrew-aiculator Scoop Commits to your bucket PACKAGING_TOKEN Repository scoop-aiculator apt, dnf, apk Signed repositories on GitHub Pages PACKAGING_TOKEN, PACKAGE_GPG_KEY, APK_SIGNING_KEY Repository aiculator-packages, with Pages on Chocolatey choco push CHOCOLATEY_API_KEY A community.chocolatey.org account WinGet Pull request to microsoft/winget-pkgs WINGET_TOKEN Nothing Arch User Repository Pushes aiculator-bin AUR_SSH_KEY An aur.archlinux.org account with this public key

apt, dnf and apk have no central registry that accepts a project directly, so these repositories are hosted by the project. Getting into Debian, Fedora or Alpine themselves means going through each distribution's own review.

Two channels have human review. Chocolatey moderates package versions before listing them, and each WinGet version is a pull request that is reviewed before it merges. Both can take days, while the other channels are live after the workflow finishes.

docs.title: Repositories
docs.text:
gh repo create Grano22/homebrew-aiculator --public --add-readme
gh repo create Grano22/scoop-aiculator --public --add-readme
gh repo create Grano22/aiculator-packages --public --add-readme
gh api -X POST repos/Grano22/aiculator-packages/pages \
  -f build_type=legacy -f 'source[branch]=master' -f 'source[path]=/'

The Pages source for aiculator-packages must be Deploy from a branch, on master at /, which is what build_type=legacy sets. With the GitHub Actions source, a publish succeeds but the URLs return 404.

docs.title: Tokens
docs.text:
• PACKAGING_TOKEN: a fine-grained token, limited to the three repositories above, with Contents: read and write.
  • WINGET_TOKEN: a classic token, because it must fork and open a pull request on a repository you do not own. See wingetcreate's token guide for its scope.
  • CHOCOLATEY_API_KEY: from your account page on community.chocolatey.org.

docs.title: Signing keys
docs.text:
Generate these on a trusted machine. They have no passphrase, because CI has to use them unattended, so the repository secret is what protects them.

export GNUPGHOME=$(mktemp -d)
gpg --batch --passphrase '' --quick-generate-key "Aiculator packages" ed25519 sign 5y
gpg --batch --armor --export-secret-keys | gh secret set PACKAGE_GPG_KEY -R Grano22/aiculator
openssl genrsa 4096 | openssl pkcs8 -topk8 -nocrypt | gh secret set APK_SIGNING_KEY -R Grano22/aiculator
ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -N '' -C aiculator-aur -f aur_ed25519
gh secret set AUR_SSH_KEY -R Grano22/aiculator < aur_ed25519

Add aur_ed25519.pub to your AUR account, then delete both files and $GNUPGHOME.

Keep a safe copy of the GPG and apk keys if you want the option to restore them. Replacing either key later means every user has to trust the new one.

docs.title: Try it without publishing
docs.text:
gh workflow run packages.yml -R Grano22/aiculator -f dry_run=true            # The latest release
gh workflow run packages.yml -R Grano22/aiculator -f tag=v0.4.0 -f dry_run=false   # Retry a release for real

A dry run installs from every channel using throwaway signing keys. Pull requests that change the packaging run one automatically. Publishing again is safe, since each channel notices a version it already has.

docs.title: Install, once published
docs.text:
macOS and LinuxWindowsDebian and UbuntuFedora and RHELAlpineArch 
brew install grano22/aiculator/aiculator

Homebrew asks you to trust third-party taps. See its tap docs.

scoop bucket add aiculator https://github.com/Grano22/scoop-aiculator
scoop install aiculator

choco install aiculator

winget install Grano22.Aiculator

sudo install -d /etc/apt/keyrings
curl -fsSL https://grano22.github.io/aiculator-packages/aiculator.gpg | sudo tee /etc/apt/keyrings/aiculator.gpg > /dev/null
echo "deb [signed-by=/etc/apt/keyrings/aiculator.gpg] https://grano22.github.io/aiculator-packages/apt stable main" | sudo tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/aiculator.list
sudo apt update && sudo apt install aiculator

sudo tee /etc/yum.repos.d/aiculator.repo > /dev/null <<'REPO'
[aiculator]
name=Aiculator
baseurl=https://grano22.github.io/aiculator-packages/rpm
enabled=1
gpgcheck=1
repo_gpgcheck=1
gpgkey=https://grano22.github.io/aiculator-packages/aiculator.asc
REPO
sudo dnf install aiculator

wget -q https://grano22.github.io/aiculator-packages/aiculator.rsa.pub -O /etc/apk/keys/aiculator.rsa.pub
echo https://grano22.github.io/aiculator-packages/apk >> /etc/apk/repositories
apk update && apk add aiculator

yay -S aiculator-bin

docs.title: Limits
docs.text:
• Windows on Arm: Chocolatey installs the x64 build. Scoop and WinGet have native arm64 builds.
  • Old versions: the apt, dnf and apk repositories keep the newest 5 versions, and keep no git history, so that they stay within GitHub Pages' size limits.
  • macOS signing: the binaries are not notarized by Apple.

docs.title: Releasing
docs.text: Releases are driven by semantic version tags. scripts/release.sh creates the tag, and pushing it does the rest.

docs.title: Make a release
docs.text:
1. Keep CHANGELOG.md current as you work, under ## [Unreleased].

  2. Preview:

    scripts/release.sh --bump minor --dry-run

  3. Create and publish:

    scripts/release.sh --bump minor --push
Flag Meaning --bump major\|minor\|patch The next version, from the latest stable tag --version X.Y.Z An exact version --pre rc.1 A prerelease, such as v1.2.0-rc.1 --push Push the commit and tag, which publishes --dry-run Show what would happen, and change nothing --allow-branch Release from a branch other than master --skip-tests Skip the local tests; CI still runs them

Without --push, nothing leaves your machine, and the script prints how to undo it.

The script refuses a version that is not semantic or already exists, an empty [Unreleased] section, and uncommitted changes.

docs.title: What a tag does
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    T[Push tag v1.2.3] --> V[Verify tag, notes and tests]
    V --> B[Build 8 platforms]
    B --> P[Publish release]
    T --> D[Publish docs 1.2 and latest]
  • Binaries: Linux, macOS, Windows and FreeBSD, each on amd64 and arm64.
  • Each archive includes the third-party license notices, which the dependency licenses require.
  • Also published: SHA256SUMS, build provenance attestations, and notes taken from that version's changelog section.
  • Prereleases are marked as such on GitHub, and do not change the latest docs.

Check an archive's provenance with:

gh attestation verify aiculator_v1.2.3_linux_amd64.tar.gz --repo OWNER/REPO

docs.title: Size budget
docs.text:
scripts/build_release.sh fails if a binary or an archive goes over budget, so neither CI nor a release can ship past it.

Package Budget Current Binary 30 MiB 24.6 to 27.7 MiB Archive 12 MiB 9.2 to 11.1 MiB

The template engine accounts for about 5.4 MiB of the binary, because real Jinja2 brings text-handling and JSON libraries with it. To raise a limit, change it in the script on purpose and say why in the commit.

docs.text: Every command, generated from the program itself. Run any command with --help to see the same text.

docs.title: aiculator agents
docs.text:
Stop or kill the agents working on the swarm

aiculator agents

docs.title: aiculator agents kill
docs.text:
Stop agents, and end the processes aiculator started for them

Stop agents, as stop does, and end the processes that aiculator itself started for them on this machine: aiculator drive and the harness it runs. A harness you started yourself, such as an open Claude Code session, is told to exit and never killed.

aiculator agents kill [AGENT...] [flags]

Flags

      --all      every agent
      --realms   in every running realm on this machine, not just this project

docs.title: aiculator agents stop
docs.text:
Tell agents to exit, and hand back what they hold

Tell agents to exit. Each gets exit from its next wait, or from the one it is in now, and what it holds goes back to the queue at once with no penalty. Its process keeps running until it reads the exit; kill also ends the processes aiculator started.

aiculator agents stop [AGENT...] [flags]

Flags

      --all      every agent
      --realms   in every running realm on this machine, not just this project

docs.title: aiculator backup
docs.text:
Keep and restore copies of chosen tasks

Keep and restore copies of chosen tasks.

Rules in .agents/backups.yaml choose tasks by id pattern, label, tag, state or priority, or all of them, and keep a journal of each change, snapshots at an interval, or both. The server keeps them while it runs; these commands read them.

aiculator backup

docs.title: aiculator backup now
docs.text:
Take a snapshot now, for one rule or all of them

aiculator backup now [RULE]

docs.title: aiculator backup restore
docs.text:
Put kept copies of tasks back

Put kept copies of tasks back.

By default each task gets its newest copy that differs from the task as it is now. --before takes the newest copy at or before a time, and --from takes the copies in one journal or snapshot file; with --all, every task in that file. Work that was in flight in a copy goes back to ready, the lease moves on so no agent with an old lease can write, and the record being replaced is kept in quarantine.

aiculator backup restore [TASK...] [flags]

Flags

      --all             with --from, every task in the file
      --before string   newest copy at or before this time: RFC 3339, a date, or a duration ago such as 2h
      --dry-run         say what would be restored, and change nothing
      --from string     restore from this journal or snapshot file

docs.title: aiculator backup status
docs.text:
Show what each backup rule has kept

aiculator backup status

docs.title: aiculator backup versions
docs.text:
List the kept copies of a task, oldest first

aiculator backup versions TASK [flags]

Flags

      --json   print JSON

docs.title: aiculator debug verbosity
docs.text:
Show or change a running server's verbosity, with no restart

Changes take effect at once. Use --for, so that a debugging session cannot leave the server logging at a high level by accident. The previous level then comes back by itself.

aiculator debug verbosity [LEVEL] [flags]

  aiculator debug verbosity 5 --for 10m         trace for ten minutes

docs.title: aiculator doctor
docs.text:
Check this project's swarm for damage and leftovers, and fix them with --fix

Checks the data directory, even with the server down: a stale pid or address file, or a server holding the lock without answering. With the server up, it also reports records repaired at startup, records kept in quarantine, worktrees of finished tasks, and leases long past their deadline.

Damaged task records are repaired when the server starts, with the originals kept. --fix removes stale files and leftover worktrees. It never deletes a task or anything kept in quarantine.

aiculator doctor [flags]

Flags

      --fix    fix what can be fixed safely
      --json   print as JSON

docs.title: aiculator events
docs.text:
Stream every task change as JSON lines

Stream every task change as JSON lines. Each line has a seq. --since SEQ starts after that one, so a consumer that saves the last seq it handled misses nothing when it starts again. With --follow, a dropped connection is resumed from the last line printed, for as long as this runs. Delivery is at least once: after a crash, dedupe by seq.

aiculator events [flags]

Examples

  aiculator events
  aiculator events --since 1200 --follow
  aiculator events | jq -r 'select(.state == "done") | .id'

Flags

      --follow       reconnect after a drop, resuming from the last event printed
      --since uint   start after this event sequence; 0 means from now

docs.title: aiculator export
docs.text:
Write tasks or other data to a file: JSON, YAML, CSV, TSV, Excel, HTML or Markdown

Exports what you choose, in the format you choose. Tasks are the default, and JSON is the default format, unless the file name in -o says otherwise.

Values are always treated as text: HTML is escaped, Excel cells are stored as strings, and in CSV a value that a spreadsheet would run as a formula starts with a quote.

aiculator export [tasks|agents|usage|flow|realms] [flags]

Examples

  aiculator export                                   # All tasks, as JSON
  aiculator export -o tasks.xlsx                     # The file name picks the format
  aiculator export --format html -o report.html --state running,review
  aiculator export --fields id,title,labels.team,owner --format csv
  aiculator export --label team=core --sort priority -o core.yaml
  aiculator export --with-meta --fields id,meta.points -o points.csv
  aiculator export --all -o everything.xlsx          # Tasks from every realm
  aiculator export --list-fields                     # What can be selected
  aiculator export realms --format md

Flags

      --all                 tasks from every running realm, with a realm column
      --fields strings      what to include, such as id,title,labels.team; see --list-fields
      --format string       json, yaml, csv, tsv, xlsx, html or md; from the file name, or json
      --label stringArray   only with this label, as name=value
      --limit int           stop after this many rows
      --list-fields         list what can be selected, and write nothing
  -o, --output string       file to write; standard output if empty
      --sort string         sort by this field; -field for descending
      --state strings       only these states, such as running,review
      --where stringArray   only where a field has this value, as field=value
      --with-meta           add each task's properties, as meta.NAME; costs one request per task

docs.title: aiculator init
docs.text:
Set up this machine, step by step: harnesses, skills and MCP config

Asks what you want, then does it. By default this sets up the whole machine: the swarm's skills go where each harness reads them for every project, so that afterwards aiculator join only has to start a server in a project. This needs no git repository and starts no server.

With --scoped it sets up this project alone, which also offers to start the server, and to create the git repository the swarm needs.

Nothing is written until the last question is answered, so backing out with Ctrl-C changes nothing. Running it again is safe, and keeps what is already there.

For a script, --yes takes every default, and flags answer single questions.

aiculator init [flags]

Flags

      --all-harnesses    also offer harnesses that were not found on this machine
      --dry-run          say what would be done, and do nothing
      --harness string   set these up without asking: installed, all, or comma-separated ids
      --mcp              add MCP config without asking
      --no-mcp           do not add MCP config
      --no-skills        do not install the skills
      --no-start         do not start the server, with --scoped
      --planner          also allow these sessions to plan
      --sandbox string   sandbox for the server: auto, seatbelt, bwrap, docker or none (default "auto")
      --scoped           set up this project only, rather than the whole machine
      --tier int         tier for MCP sessions: 1 standard, 2 advanced, 3 ultra (default 1)
  -y, --yes              take every default and ask nothing

docs.title: aiculator join
docs.text:
Connect installed harnesses to the swarm: server, skills and MCP config

Sets a project up so any harness can join the swarm, including one already open.

It starts the server, and works on its own on a machine with nothing set up: it installs the bundled skills into .agents/skills, links them to harnesses that need it, and registers the MCP bridge. Anything a harness can already find is left alone, at either level, so after aiculator init it only has to start the server. No secrets are written.

aiculator join [flags]

Flags

      --harness string   installed, all, or comma-separated ids (default "installed")
      --no-start         do not start the server
      --planner          also allow these sessions to plan
      --sandbox string   sandbox for the server: auto, seatbelt, bwrap, docker or none (default "auto")
      --tier int         tier: 1 standard, 2 advanced, 3 ultra (default 1)

docs.title: aiculator parallel
docs.text:
Work out what subagents can do at the same time in one working tree

Worktrees keep tasks apart. This is the level below: one task split among subagents in one checkout. Give it the jobs and what each will change, and it says what can safely run at once. Jobs share a wave only if their claims cannot overlap, and a job that claims nothing runs alone.

This needs no server, and it does not touch the swarm's state.

aiculator parallel

docs.title: aiculator parallel plan
docs.text:
Plan jobs into waves that cannot conflict

Reads jobs as YAML or JSON. A claim is a file or a directory ending in /. With symbol granularity it can also be file#symbol or file:10-40. Reads are what a job relies on staying the same while it works.

Granularity is how finely claims are compared. The default, auto, uses the coarser of dir and file that loses no parallelism, and it treats file#symbol as the whole file. To let two jobs share one file, ask for symbol. Their claims are then checked against the file, but nothing can stop a subagent straying, and two in one file can overwrite each other.

aiculator parallel plan [flags]

Examples

  aiculator parallel plan --file jobs.yaml -o plan.json
  cat jobs.yaml | aiculator parallel plan --file - --max 3

  # jobs.yaml
  jobs:
    - id: api
      touches: [internal/api/users.go]
    - id: docs
      touches: [docs/users.md]
      reads: [internal/api/users.go]
    - id: format
      exclusive: true
      deps: [api, docs]

Flags

      --file string          the jobs, as YAML or JSON; - for standard input
      --granularity string   dir, file, symbol, repo or auto (default "auto")
      --json                 print the plan as JSON
      --max int              most subagents at once (default 4)
  -o, --output string        save the plan, for verify

docs.title: aiculator skill
docs.text:
Manage skills in one place: .agents/skills

Skills live in .agents/skills. Installing puts them where each harness looks: harnesses that scan .agents/skills need nothing, and the others get a link. Skills in .agent/skills are picked up too. An edit in one place reaches every harness.

Patterns use * for anything, ? for one character and [abc] for a set. Quote any pattern with a wildcard: an unquoted * alone also works, but zsh stops at an unmatched *-sth.

aiculator skill [--install PATTERN...] [flags]

Examples

  aiculator skill --install '*'                  all skills, to every installed harness
  aiculator skill --install 'swarm-*' 'lint-?'   by pattern
  aiculator skill --install '*-tool' --global    into ~/.agents/skills and home directories
  aiculator skill --install '*' --harness all    every supported harness, installed or not
  aiculator skill --install x --harness claude,pi
  aiculator skill --install x --path ./vendor/skills --harness none
  aiculator skill --install x --source ~/my-skills
  aiculator skill --list
  aiculator skill --lint
  aiculator skill --new my-skill --description "..."
  aiculator skill --uninstall 'swarm-*' --purge

Flags

      --copy                 copy instead of linking, for tools that do not follow links
      --description string   description for --new
      --force                refresh bundled skills and replace links; your own directories are never replaced
      --global               use ~/.agents/skills and home directories
      --harness string       installed, all, none, or comma-separated ids (default "installed")
      --install strings      install skills matching these patterns
      --lint                 check skills against the Agent Skills spec
      --list                 list skills

docs.title: aiculator template
docs.text:
Render reusable instruction templates into skills

Templates live in .agents/templates; .agent/templates and .agent/template also work. They use Jinja2 and MDX-style components, and render into skills that install exactly as aiculator skill --install does.

Bundled components: Directive, Anchor, Subagents, Backoff, OutputFormat, Flow, Step, Note, Toc. Add or replace one by creating components/NAME.md in a template directory.

These produce instructions for a model. A model can still ignore text, so anything that must hold needs a real check, such as a task's --check command.

aiculator template [--install PATTERN...] [flags]

Examples

  aiculator template --list
  aiculator template --new my-rules
  aiculator template --render agent-discipline --set retries=5
  aiculator template --install '*'
  aiculator template --install 'agent-*' --global --set timeout=300s
  aiculator template --install x --per-harness       a separate copy per harness
  aiculator template --install x --path ./vendor/skills --harness none
  aiculator template --check                         fail if a rendered skill is stale

Flags

      --check             fail if a rendered skill no longer matches its template
      --copy              copy instead of linking
      --for string        with --render, render as this harness
      --force             replace links; your own directories are never replaced
      --global            use ~/.agents and home directories
      --harness string    installed, all, none, or comma-separated ids (default "installed")
      --install strings   render and install templates matching these patterns
      --list              list templates
      --new string        create a starter template
      --path strings      also install to this directory
      --per-harness       render a separate copy into each harness's own directory
      --render string     print one rendered template; writes nothing
      --set stringArray   template variable, as KEY=VALUE
      --source strings    also read templates from this directory

docs.title: aiculator top
docs.text:
Live terminal dashboard: flow, throughput, latency, jitter, probes, liveness and usage

A live view of the swarm. Keys: 1-5 or tab switch views, arrows or j and k scroll, r turns live mode on and off, p pauses, q quits. Live mode redraws four times a second, so a change shows as it happens; --live starts in it.

Without a terminal, such as in a pipe, it prints one frame and exits. Rates reset when the server restarts. Task states and usage totals do not.

aiculator top [flags]

Flags

      --all                 show every realm on this machine: 1 realms, 2 tasks, 3 agents
      --color               with --once: keep color even in a pipe
      --interval duration   how often to refresh (default 1s)
      --json                print the raw snapshot as JSON and exit
      --live                start in live mode, redrawing four times a second; r toggles it
      --no-color            no color; NO_COLOR also works
      --once                print one frame and exit
      --view string         with --once: overview, tasks, sessions, flow or usage (default "overview")
      --width int           with --once: width in columns
